name: @0gzk/mcp

tools.name: search_circuits
tools.description: Search 0gzk ZK circuits by natural-language query (matched against names, tags, keywords, use cases, and descriptions). In repo mode this searches the local catalog; without a repo it falls back to substring-matching circuit names on a live registry.

query.description: What the circuit should do, e.g. "prove age over 18"

chain.description: Only report publications on this chain (catalog mode) / registry to enumerate (discovery mode)

tools.name: list_circuits
tools.description: List known circuits. source=catalog lists the local repo catalog (name/version/description/tags/publications); source=registry pages through the live on-chain registry for a chain.

source.description: Defaults to catalog; falls back to registry when no catalog is available

tools.name: get_circuit
tools.description: Get the full record for one circuit: metadata (inputs/outputs), constraints, example input, publications, and how to prove with it. Unknown names can be resolved from a live registry and their published bundle fetched into the local cache.

chain.description: Registry chain for non-catalog circuits (default base)

fetchIfMissing.description: Allow downloading the published bundle when the circuit is not in the catalog

tools.name: get_example_input
tools.description: Get the committed example_input.json for a catalog circuit — the fastest way to see a valid input shape.

tools.name: resolve_circuit
tools.description: Resolve a "name" or "name@version" spec against the on-chain registries and report the published record per chain (rootHash, vkeyHash, verifier, publisher, publishedAt).

tools.name: validate_inputs
tools.description: Check a set of user-supplied circuit inputs against the circuit's declared signal schema WITHOUT proving. Returns {valid, errors, schema}. Call this before prove_circuit whenever the user supplies values: it is instant, it never downloads a bundle when the circuit is in the catalog, and its errors name the exact signal and expected type. Also use it (with no inputs) to show a user what a circuit needs.

inputs.description: Candidate inputs keyed by signal name; omit to just fetch the expected schema

chain.description: Registry chain used only when the circuit is not in the catalog

tools.name: read_input_file
tools.description: Read a JSON file of circuit inputs from the user's machine so it can be validated and proved. Returns only the SIGNAL NAMES and value types found — never the values themselves, which stay local. Use it when a user references a file instead of typing values, then pass the same path to prove_circuit via inputFile.

path.description: Path to a JSON file containing circuit inputs

tools.name: prove_circuit
tools.description: Generate a Groth16 proof (and locally verify it) for a circuit, optionally saving the artifacts to disk. Bundle source: a repo circuit's circuit_bundle/ by name (falling back to the published registry bundle), an explicit bundleDir, or a published rootHash fetched into the cache. Input validation errors describe the exact expected input schema. Proving runs wherever this tool executes — the witness never leaves that machine.

inputs.description: Circuit inputs keyed by signal name (field elements as decimal strings)

inputFile.description: Path to a JSON file of inputs, read locally — use instead of `inputs` to keep values off the wire

name.description: Circuit name (repo circuit_bundle/ preferred, registry fallback)

outDir.description: Directory for proof.json, public.json and result.json. Defaults to ~/.0gzk/proofs/<circuit>-<timestamp>/. The absolute path is always returned as saved.outDir.
